title: America's AI Action Plan — Phase 65 AI for science review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the AI for science reporting pack. The AI Action Plan lays out more than 90 federal actions under innovation, infrastructure, and international security pillars. It treats AI leadership as a full-stack problem involving models, scientific data, chips, data centers, power, permitting, workforce, cybersecurity, exports, and secure government compute.
key_findings: AI infrastructure policy includes data centers, semiconductor fabs, reliable power, grid expansion, and skilled trades.
The plan calls for AI-enabled science, high-quality datasets, evaluation, security, and adoption across government.
International policy is framed around exporting complete U.S. AI stacks rather than isolated software.
why_it_matters: Which records connect compute, data, evaluation, and program support to institutional adoption, reproduced scientific work, and measured research outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It makes the physical and institutional dependencies of AI unusually explicit and provides actions that can be monitored for implementation.
ftfn_relevance: Creates dated follow-up lanes for federal standards, infrastructure, procurement, and export programs.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The plan contains recommendations and directives at different stages of implementation.
It does not establish that grid capacity, fabs, data centers, workforce, or secure compute have been delivered.
